sections.heading: Coverage Indications, Limitations, and/or Medical Necessity
sections.text:
Indications for Coverage
This section describes the indications for which nerve conduction studies may be covered.
Nerve conduction studies may be covered for beneficiaries with suspected carpal tunnel syndrome. Nerve conduction studies may be covered for beneficiaries with suspected myasthenia gravis. Nerve conduction studies may be covered for beneficiaries with suspected motor neuron disease. Nerve conduction studies may be covered for beneficiaries with suspected radiculopathy.
Medical Necessity Criteria
Coverage requires that all of the following criteria are met:
1. The beneficiary has been evaluated in person by the treating practitioner within the past 30 days.
2. Conservative treatment has been tried and has not produced adequate improvement.
3. Symptoms have persisted for at least 4 weeks.
Non-Covered Services
The following limitations apply:
Studies interpreted by a practitioner without electrodiagnostic training are not covered. Routine repeat studies without a change in clinical status are not covered.
Provider Qualifications
The following qualifications apply:
1. The ordering practitioner must be enrolled in Medicare.
2. Services must be performed by personnel who are licensed or certified to perform nerve conduction studies under state law.
3. Nerve conduction studies must be ordered by a physician or non-physician practitioner who is treating the beneficiary for peripheral nerve disorders.
4. Nerve conduction studies must be furnished under general supervision of a physician.

sections.heading: Associated Information
sections.text:
Frequency and Duration
No more than 2 studies of the same nerve are covered within a 6-month period.
Documentation Requirements for the Medical Record
The medical record must support the medical necessity of each service.
- Documentation must describe prior treatments attempted and the outcome of each.
- The medical record must include the diagnosis that supports medical necessity.
- Progress notes must document the beneficiary's response to each study.
- Results of a neurological examination relied upon to establish medical necessity must be available in the medical record.
- Documentation must identify the practitioner who performed or supervised each study.

sections.heading: ICD-10-CM Codes that Support Medical Necessity
sections.text:
The following ICD-10-CM codes support medical necessity for nerve conduction studies:
1. E11.42 - Type 2 diabetes mellitus with diabetic polyneuropathy
2. G56.02 - Carpal tunnel syndrome, left upper limb
3. M54.12 - Radiculopathy, cervical region

sections.heading: Billing and Coding Guidelines
sections.text:
The following billing instructions apply:
- Services that do not meet the criteria in this policy should be reported with the modifier indicating that denial is expected.
- Report the date of the initial study on the claim.
- Telehealth delivery of nerve conduction studies is not separately billable under this policy.

sections.heading: Applicability
sections.text: The requirements of this policy apply to services performed on or after 03/01/2019.

sections.text: Fictional Society of Neurology. Clinical practice guideline for peripheral nerve disorders. 2017 edition.

sections.heading: Coverage Indications
sections.text:
This section describes the indications for which nerve conduction studies may be covered.
1. Nerve conduction studies may be covered for beneficiaries with suspected peripheral polyneuropathy.
2. Nerve conduction studies may be covered for beneficiaries with suspected motor neuron disease.
3. Nerve conduction studies may be covered for beneficiaries with suspected ulnar neuropathy.
4. Nerve conduction studies may be covered for beneficiaries with suspected carpal tunnel syndrome.

sections.heading: Eligibility Criteria
sections.text:
The beneficiary must meet each of the following criteria:
1. Symptoms have persisted for at least 4 weeks.
2. Conservative treatment has been tried and has not produced adequate improvement.
3. The beneficiary has a documented diagnosis of peripheral nerve disorders.
4. The beneficiary has been evaluated in person by the treating practitioner within the past 90 days.

sections.heading: Limitations and Exclusions
sections.text:
The following limitations apply:
- Studies performed with devices that do not produce waveforms are not covered.
- Testing performed solely to establish a baseline before surgery is not covered.
- Screening studies in asymptomatic beneficiaries are not covered.

sections.heading: Utilization Guidelines
sections.text:
The following frequency and duration limits apply:
No more than 1 studies of the same nerve are covered within a 6-month period.

sections.heading: Clinical Evidence Required for Coverage
sections.text: Results of a neurological examination obtained within 12 months before the initial study must be available.

sections.heading: Documentation Requirements
sections.text:
The medical record must support the medical necessity of each service.
- Results of a neurological examination relied upon to establish medical necessity must be available in the medical record.
- The medical record must include the diagnosis that supports medical necessity.
- The medical record must contain a signed and dated order for nerve conduction studies from the treating practitioner.

sections.heading: Practitioner Qualifications and Supervision
sections.text:
The following qualifications apply:
- Services must be performed by personnel who are licensed or certified to perform nerve conduction studies under state law.
- Staff furnishing nerve conduction studies must hold current basic life support certification.
- Nerve conduction studies must be furnished under direct supervision of a physician.

sections.heading: Billing Instructions
sections.text:

sections.heading: Coverage Indications, Limitations, and/or Medical Necessity
sections.text:
Indications for Coverage
Nerve conduction studies is covered when the requirements of this policy are met.
1. Coverage of nerve conduction studies is provided for beneficiaries with suspected motor neuron disease.
2. Coverage of nerve conduction studies is provided for beneficiaries with suspected peripheral polyneuropathy.
3. Coverage of nerve conduction studies is provided for beneficiaries with suspected carpal tunnel syndrome.
4. Coverage of nerve conduction studies is provided for beneficiaries with suspected ulnar neuropathy.
Patient Selection Criteria
The beneficiary must meet each of the following criteria:
Symptoms have persisted for at least 3 weeks. The treating practitioner expects measurable improvement within a predictable period. The beneficiary is able to understand and participate in the plan of care. The beneficiary has been evaluated in person by the treating practitioner within the past 60 days.
Limitations
The following limitations apply:
1. Studies performed with devices that do not produce waveforms are not covered.
2. Testing performed solely to establish a baseline before surgery is not covered.
3. Routine repeat studies without a change in clinical status are not covered.
Clinical Evidence Required for Coverage
Results of a neurological examination obtained within 6 months before the initial study must be available.
Practitioner Qualifications and Supervision
- The performing practitioner must have documented training and experience in nerve conduction studies.
- Staff furnishing nerve conduction studies must hold current basic life support certification.
- Nerve conduction studies must be furnished under direct supervision of a physician.

sections.heading: Associated Information
sections.text:
Frequency and Duration
No more than 1 studies of the same nerve are covered within a 6-month period.
Documentation Requirements for the Medical Record
The following documentation must be available upon request:
- Documentation must identify the practitioner who performed or supervised each study.
- When nerve conduction studies continues beyond the initial period, the record must document measurable improvement.
- Documentation must describe prior treatments attempted and the outcome of each.

sections.heading: Covered Diagnosis Codes (ICD-10-CM)
sections.text:
Claims must include one of the following ICD-10-CM codes:
1. E11.42 - Type 2 diabetes mellitus with diabetic polyneuropathy
2. G56.02 - Carpal tunnel syndrome, left upper limb
3. G62.9 - Polyneuropathy, unspecified

sections.heading: Billing and Coding Guidelines
sections.text:
1. Services that do not meet the criteria in this policy should be reported with the modifier indicating that denial is expected.
2. Report one unit of service for each study furnished.

sections.heading: Summary of Evidence and Rationale
sections.text: Published studies report improvements in diagnostic accuracy among beneficiaries receiving nerve conduction studies. Evidence for benefit is strongest when nerve conduction studies is combined with ongoing medical management.

sections.heading: Sources of Information
sections.text: Example Journal of Neurology. Outcomes of nerve conduction studies in older adults. 2019.

The study is directed to the specific nerves implicated by the examination. A clinical history and examination support the need for testing. Conservative treatment has been tried and has not produced adequate improvement. Symptoms have persisted for at least 4 weeks.

Nerve conduction studies must be furnished under direct supervision of a physician.

sections.heading: Associated Information
sections.text:

- Documentation must describe prior treatments attempted and the outcome of each.
- When nerve conduction studies continues beyond the initial period, the record must document measurable improvement.
- A plan of care that specifies goals, frequency and expected duration must be on file before nerve conduction studies begins.
- Results of a neurological examination relied upon to establish medical necessity must be available in the medical record.
- The medical record must contain a signed and dated order for nerve conduction studies from the treating practitioner.

- Nerve conduction studies is considered reasonable and necessary for beneficiaries with suspected carpal tunnel syndrome.
- Nerve conduction studies is considered reasonable and necessary for beneficiaries with suspected radiculopathy.
Eligibility Criteria
Coverage requires that all of the following criteria are met:
- The beneficiary has a documented diagnosis of peripheral nerve disorders.
- Symptoms have persisted for at least 3 weeks.
- The beneficiary has been evaluated in person by the treating practitioner within the past 60 days.
- Conservative treatment has been tried and has not produced adequate improvement.
Non-Covered Services
The following limitations apply:
1. Studies interpreted by a practitioner without electrodiagnostic training are not covered.
2. Screening studies in asymptomatic beneficiaries are not covered.
Clinical Evidence Required for Coverage
The following clinical evidence is required:
Results of a neurological examination obtained within 6 months before the initial study must be available.
Provider Qualifications
1. Nerve conduction studies must be ordered by a physician or non-physician practitioner who is treating the beneficiary for peripheral nerve disorders.
2. The ordering practitioner must be enrolled in Medicare.

The following frequency and duration limits apply:
No more than 1 studies of the same nerve are covered within a 6-month period.

sections.heading: Coverage Indications, Limitations, and/or Medical Necessity
sections.text:
Indications for Coverage
Nerve conduction studies is covered when the requirements of this policy are met.
- Coverage of nerve conduction studies is provided for beneficiaries with suspected peripheral polyneuropathy.
- Coverage of nerve conduction studies is provided for beneficiaries with suspected myasthenia gravis.
- Coverage of nerve conduction studies is provided for beneficiaries with suspected motor neuron disease.
- Coverage of nerve conduction studies is provided for beneficiaries with suspected ulnar neuropathy.
Medical Necessity Criteria
The beneficiary must meet each of the following criteria:
1. The results are expected to change diagnosis or management.
2. Conservative treatment has been tried and has not produced adequate improvement.
3. Symptoms have persisted for at least 3 weeks.
4. The treating practitioner expects measurable improvement within a predictable period.
Limitations
The following limitations apply:
1. Routine repeat studies without a change in clinical status are not covered.
2. Screening studies in asymptomatic beneficiaries are not covered.
3. Testing performed solely to establish a baseline before surgery is not covered.
Required Testing
The following clinical evidence is required:
1. Results of a neurological examination obtained within 3 months before the initial study must be available.
2. A baseline result from a neurological examination must be recorded before the initial study.
Provider Qualifications
The following qualifications apply:
- Staff furnishing nerve conduction studies must hold current basic life support certification.
- Facilities furnishing nerve conduction studies must maintain written protocols for emergency response.
- The interpreting practitioner must be board certified in neurology.
- Nerve conduction studies must be furnished under direct supervision of a physician.

sections.heading: Associated Information
sections.text:
Frequency and Duration
No more than 1 studies of the same nerve are covered within a 6-month period.
Documentation Requirements
The following documentation must be available upon request:
1. Results of a neurological examination relied upon to establish medical necessity must be available in the medical record.
2. The medical record must contain a signed and dated order for nerve conduction studies from the treating practitioner.
3. Documentation must describe prior treatments attempted and the outcome of each.
4. The medical record must include the diagnosis that supports medical necessity.
5. The record must include a signed attestation that the beneficiary received education about nerve conduction studies.

sections.heading: Coverage Indications, Limitations, and/or Medical Necessity
sections.text:
Indications for Coverage
This section describes the indications for which nerve conduction studies may be covered.
- Coverage of nerve conduction studies is provided for beneficiaries with suspected myasthenia gravis.
- Coverage of nerve conduction studies is provided for beneficiaries with suspected ulnar neuropathy.
- Coverage of nerve conduction studies is provided for beneficiaries with suspected carpal tunnel syndrome.
- Coverage of nerve conduction studies is provided for beneficiaries with suspected radiculopathy.
Eligibility Criteria
Coverage requires that all of the following criteria are met:
- Symptoms have persisted for at least 3 weeks.
- The beneficiary is able to understand and participate in the plan of care.
- The beneficiary has been evaluated in person by the treating practitioner within the past 90 days.
- Conservative treatment has been tried and has not produced adequate improvement.
Limitations and Exclusions
The following are not considered reasonable and necessary:
Routine repeat studies without a change in clinical status are not covered. Studies interpreted by a practitioner without electrodiagnostic training are not covered. Testing performed solely to establish a baseline before surgery is not covered.
Clinical Evidence Required for Coverage
Results of a neurological examination obtained within 6 months before the initial study must be available.
Practitioner Qualifications and Supervision
1. The interpreting practitioner must be board certified in neurology.
2. The performing practitioner must have documented training and experience in nerve conduction studies.
3. Services must be performed by personnel who are licensed or certified to perform nerve conduction studies under state law.
4. Nerve conduction studies must be furnished under direct supervision of a physician.

sections.heading: Associated Information
sections.text:
Utilization Guidelines
The following frequency and duration limits apply:
No more than 2 studies of the same nerve are covered within a 6-month period.
Documentation Requirements for the Medical Record
The following documentation must be available upon request:
- A plan of care that specifies goals, frequency and expected duration must be on file before nerve conduction studies begins.
- The treating practitioner must document a face-to-face evaluation within 30 days before the initial study.
- The medical record must contain a signed and dated order for nerve conduction studies from the treating practitioner.
- The medical record must include the diagnosis that supports medical necessity.

sections.heading: Covered Diagnosis Codes (ICD-10-CM)
sections.text:
Claims must include one of the following ICD-10-CM codes:
1. E11.42 - Type 2 diabetes mellitus with diabetic polyneuropathy
2. G56.01 - Carpal tunnel syndrome, right upper limb
3. G62.9 - Polyneuropathy, unspecified

sections.heading: Billing and Coding Guidelines
sections.text:
The following billing instructions apply:
The ICD-10-CM code that supports medical necessity must be reported on the claim. Report one unit of service for each study furnished. Services must be billed with the place of service code that reflects where the study was furnished. Services that do not meet the criteria in this policy should be reported with the modifier indicating that denial is expected.

sections.text: The requirements of this policy apply to services performed on or after 04/01/2025.

sections.heading: Coverage Indications, Limitations, and/or Medical Necessity
sections.text:
Covered Indications
Nerve conduction studies is covered when the requirements of this policy are met.
1. Coverage of nerve conduction studies is provided for beneficiaries with suspected motor neuron disease.
2. Coverage of nerve conduction studies is provided for beneficiaries with suspected peripheral polyneuropathy.
3. Coverage of nerve conduction studies is provided for beneficiaries with suspected radiculopathy.
4. Coverage of nerve conduction studies is provided for beneficiaries with suspected myasthenia gravis.
Patient Selection Criteria
The beneficiary must meet each of the following criteria:
- Symptoms have persisted for at least 6 weeks.
- The study is directed to the specific nerves implicated by the examination.
- Conservative treatment has been tried and has not produced adequate improvement.
Limitations and Exclusions
The following are not considered reasonable and necessary:
Studies interpreted by a practitioner without electrodiagnostic training are not covered. Studies performed with devices that do not produce waveforms are not covered.
Provider Qualifications
The following qualifications apply:
1. The interpreting practitioner must be board certified in neurology.
2. Facilities furnishing nerve conduction studies must maintain written protocols for emergency response.
3. Nerve conduction studies must be furnished under general supervision of a physician.

sections.heading: Associated Information
sections.text:
Frequency and Duration
No more than 1 studies of the same nerve are covered within a 6-month period.
Documentation Requirements
The following documentation must be available upon request:
1. Results of a neurological examination relied upon to establish medical necessity must be available in the medical record.
2. When nerve conduction studies continues beyond the initial period, the record must document measurable improvement.
3. The record must include a signed attestation that the beneficiary received education about nerve conduction studies.
4. Documentation must state the clinical reason any study was missed or discontinued.

sections.heading: ICD-10-CM Codes that Support Medical Necessity
sections.text:
The following ICD-10-CM codes support medical necessity for nerve conduction studies:
1. G56.02 - Carpal tunnel syndrome, left upper limb
2. G62.9 - Polyneuropathy, unspecified
3. M54.12 - Radiculopathy, cervical region

sections.heading: Billing and Coding Guidelines
sections.text:
The following billing instructions apply:
Services that do not meet the criteria in this policy should be reported with the modifier indicating that denial is expected. Services must be billed with the place of service code that reflects where the study was furnished.

sections.heading: Summary of Evidence and Rationale
sections.text: Studies with longer follow-up show that benefits decline without continued adherence. The evidence reviewed consists primarily of randomized controlled trials and prospective cohort studies. Published studies report improvements in diagnostic accuracy among beneficiaries receiving nerve conduction studies.

sections.heading: Implementation
sections.text: The requirements of this policy apply to services performed on or after 09/01/2024.

sections.heading: Coverage Indications, Limitations, and/or Medical Necessity
sections.text:
Indications for Coverage
This section describes the indications for which nerve conduction studies may be covered.
1. Coverage of nerve conduction studies is provided for beneficiaries with suspected carpal tunnel syndrome.
2. Coverage of nerve conduction studies is provided for beneficiaries with suspected radiculopathy.
3. Coverage of nerve conduction studies is provided for beneficiaries with suspected ulnar neuropathy.
4. Coverage of nerve conduction studies is provided for beneficiaries with suspected motor neuron disease.
Medical Necessity Criteria
Coverage requires that all of the following criteria are met:
- Symptoms have persisted for at least 4 weeks.
- The study is directed to the specific nerves implicated by the examination.
- A clinical history and examination support the need for testing.
- The beneficiary has been evaluated in person by the treating practitioner within the past 60 days.
Non-Covered Services
The following are not considered reasonable and necessary:
1. Studies interpreted by a practitioner without electrodiagnostic training are not covered.
2. Routine repeat studies without a change in clinical status are not covered.
Practitioner Qualifications and Supervision
1. Staff furnishing nerve conduction studies must hold current basic life support certification.
2. Facilities furnishing nerve conduction studies must maintain written protocols for emergency response.
3. Nerve conduction studies must be furnished under direct supervision of a physician.

sections.heading: Associated Information
sections.text:
Frequency and Duration
No more than 1 studies of the same nerve are covered within a 6-month period.
Documentation Requirements for the Medical Record
The following documentation must be available upon request:
A plan of care that specifies goals, frequency and expected duration must be on file before nerve conduction studies begins. The medical record must contain a signed and dated order for nerve conduction studies from the treating practitioner. The record must include a signed attestation that the beneficiary received education about nerve conduction studies.

sections.heading: Covered Diagnosis Codes (ICD-10-CM)
sections.text:
Claims must include one of the following ICD-10-CM codes:
1. E11.42 - Type 2 diabetes mellitus with diabetic polyneuropathy
2. G56.01 - Carpal tunnel syndrome, right upper limb
3. M54.12 - Radiculopathy, cervical region

sections.heading: Billing Instructions
sections.text:
1. Report the date of the initial study on the claim.
2. Claims for nerve conduction studies furnished on the same date of service by the same provider should be combined on a single claim line.
3. Services that do not meet the criteria in this policy should be reported with the modifier indicating that denial is expected.
4. Claims submitted without the ordering practitioner's National Provider Identifier will be rejected.

sections.heading: Summary of Evidence and Rationale
sections.text: Evidence for benefit is strongest when nerve conduction studies is combined with ongoing medical management. The evidence reviewed consists primarily of randomized controlled trials and prospective cohort studies. Studies with longer follow-up show that benefits decline without continued adherence.

sections.heading: Implementation
sections.text: This policy applies to claims with dates of service on or after 03/01/2019.

sections.heading: Sources of Information
sections.text: Example Journal of Neurology. Outcomes of nerve conduction studies in older adults. 2022.
